items.title: Indonesian shares slump again after MSCI warns of index downgrade
items.why: Jakarta's main share index fell more than 5% on Monday to a six-year low, after an 11.6% drop on Friday, its worst day since 1998. Index provider MSCI has proposed moving Indonesia from 'emerging' to 'standalone' market status, citing opaque share ownership and suspected coordinated trading.
items.matters: A downgrade could force global index funds to sell Indonesian shares; the rupiah is near its record low against the dollar.

items.title: UN food agency cuts aid to half a million people in Gaza
items.why: The UN World Food Programme said on Monday it will stop monthly food aid for about 500,000 people in Gaza because of a funding shortfall, cutting its caseload from 1.6 million to 1.1 million. It says about two-thirds of Gazans are acutely food insecure.
items.matters: The WFP blames lower donor funding as winter nears; Israel's military aid body, COGAT, says Gaza is well supplied.

items.title: China's economy grows 4.5% in third quarter, slightly beating forecasts
items.why: China's economy grew 4.5% year on year in July–September, official figures showed on Monday, up from 4.3% in the previous quarter and just above the 4.4% economists expected. Retail sales rose 1.1% in September, while investment in property development fell 20.6% in the first nine months.
items.matters: Growth relies on strong exports while shoppers stay cautious, which matters for the many countries that trade with China.

items.title: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro trade insults in first Brazil run-off debate
items.why: Brazil's President Lula and right-wing Senator Flávio Bolsonaro met on Sunday night in São Paulo for their first debate before the 25 October run-off. They accused each other of corruption and clashed over security, healthcare and the economy. AFP says two polls this week put Bolsonaro ahead 51% to 49%.
items.matters: The winner will lead Latin America's largest country; a second and final TV debate is scheduled for Friday 23 October.

items.title: Anthropic commits 5% of its shares to a new public benefit fund
items.why: US AI company Anthropic, maker of the Claude chatbot, said on 18 October it will put 5% of its shares into a new fund for public-good projects, subject to shareholder approval. Its board may add 2% for every 50% rise in the company's value.
items.matters: Anthropic says the fund could support people affected by AI-driven job changes; it cannot be used for lobbying or political donations.

items.title: Venezuela's opposition reaffirms exiled Nobel laureate Machado as its leader
items.why: Venezuela's main opposition alliance, meeting in Caracas on Sunday, backed exiled Nobel Peace Prize laureate María Corina Machado as leader and set out 14 proposals for restoring democracy, including freeing all political prisoners. It called for free elections but set no date; Machado's party wants a vote in 2027.
items.matters: Interim President Delcy Rodríguez has led Venezuela since the US removed Nicolás Maduro in January; separate talks with the opposition exclude her.

items.title: Kenya confirms eighth Ebola case as Congo outbreak reaches new province
items.why: Kenya's health ministry confirmed an eighth Ebola case on Sunday: a 49-year-old man who worked as an attendant near the country's first patient and was already in quarantine. Four cases were confirmed on Saturday, three of them health workers. Congo says the virus has reached an eighth province.
items.matters: The Bundibugyo strain has no approved vaccine or treatment; AP says Congo's outbreak has killed at least 4,000 people since May.

items.title: Trump endorses Netanyahu nine days before Israel's 27 October election
items.why: US President Donald Trump endorsed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Sunday, saying that if Israel chose anyone else, America would have to deal with Iran itself. Polls show a tight race; AFP reports neither Netanyahu's bloc nor Gadi Eisenkot's is on course for a 61-seat majority.
items.matters: It is Israel's first national election since the Hamas-led attack of 7 October 2023.

items.title: UN nature summit opens in Armenia with most targets off track
items.why: Nearly 200 countries are meeting in Armenia's capital, Yerevan, for two weeks of UN biodiversity talks, COP17, the first review of a 2022 pact to halt nature loss by 2030. Opening the conference, Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said countries are "not yet on track".
items.matters: A UN report says current plans would protect only 26% of land and 12% of oceans by 2030, against a 30% goal.

items.title: Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff unhurt after gunmen fire at his car
items.why: Gunmen fired at actor Tiger Shroff's car in Mumbai's Juhu area, India, on the evening of 18 October, police say. He was unhurt; his driver and an autorickshaw driver were injured. Police say three suspects were arrested at Kota railway station in Rajasthan on 19 October.
items.matters: A social media post claimed the attack for the Lawrence Bishnoi gang; police say they have not verified it.

items.title: Sergei Loznitsa's Soviet-era documentary Imperium wins top London Film Festival prize
items.why: Imperium, a 175-minute documentary built from footage Italian cameramen shot in the Soviet Union in the early 1970s, won Best Film at the BFI London Film Festival on 18 October. Thailand's 9 Temples to Heaven won the best first feature award.
items.matters: Concrete Land, about a family facing displacement in Jordan, won the festival's documentary prize, the Grierson Award.

items.title: Japan set to launch probe to bring back samples from Mars moon
items.why: Japan's space agency JAXA plans to launch its MMX probe on an H3 rocket from Tanegashima at 19:41 UTC on 19 October (04:41 Tuesday, Japan time). It should reach Mars in 2027, collect at least 10 grams from the moon Phobos, and return them in 2031.
items.matters: No mission has yet brought back material from the Mars system; it may show how Mars's two small moons formed.

items.title: Ukrainian drone attack sets St Petersburg oil sites on fire
items.why: Russia's defence ministry says it downed 1,015 Ukrainian drones overnight into Sunday, one of Kyiv's largest attacks. St Petersburg's governor says an oil export terminal and a depot caught fire and one person was killed. It came two days after President Trump waived new sanctions on Russia.
items.matters: Ukraine is stepping up strikes on Russian oil despite US objections, as peace efforts stall.

items.title: Stampede at Durga Puja pavilion in India's Kolkata kills at least 19
items.why: A crowd surged as rain began outside a Durga Puja festival pavilion in Kolkata, eastern India, on Saturday evening. Indian media report at least 19 people died and about 25 were injured. Police have arrested seven people, including organisers.
items.matters: West Bengal's Chief Minister, Suvendu Adhikari, has ordered an investigation led by a sitting Calcutta High Court judge.

items.title: Rain washes out decider; India and West Indies draw T20 series 2-2
items.why: The fifth and final T20 international in Bengaluru, India, was abandoned on 17 October after India reached 118 for 5 in 7.4 overs of a match cut to nine overs a side. West Indies captain Shai Hope, with two centuries, was player of the series.
items.matters: West Indies have not won a bilateral series in India since 2002-03, ANI reports.

items.changed: Updated: Davidovich Fokina beat Jodar in Sunday's final
items.title: Spain's Davidovich Fokina beats Jodar to win Shanghai Masters title
items.why: Alejandro Davidovich Fokina came from a set and a break down to beat fellow Spaniard Rafael Jodar, 20, 1-6, 7-6, 6-4 in Shanghai, China, on 18 October. It is the 27-year-old's first Masters 1000 title; he had lost his first five career finals.
items.matters: He rises to a career-high 13th in the world; Jodar, who began the season ranked 168th, climbs to 11th.

items.title: Tonga record first win over England at Rugby League World Cup
items.why: Tonga beat England 30-12 in Perth, Australia, on 17 October in both teams' opening match of the Rugby League World Cup, before a sell-out crowd of 18,302. AP says Tonga had never beaten England before.
items.matters: Only two of the six teams in the group reach the semi-finals; England must now beat France and Papua New Guinea.

items.changed: Updated: Chwalinska beat Kartal in Sunday's final
items.title: Poland's Maja Chwalinska beats Britain's Sonay Kartal to win Wuhan Open
items.why: Maja Chwalinska came from a set down to beat Sonay Kartal 2-6, 6-4, 6-2 in Wuhan, China, on 18 October, winning her first title on the WTA tour. Kartal, ranked 170th, was the lowest-ranked finalist at this level since 2009.
items.matters: Chwalinska, ranked 146th in January, rises to 11th; Kartal climbs to about 50th and becomes British number one.

items.title: IMF meetings in Bangkok end with warnings on debt and inflation
items.why: The IMF and World Bank annual meetings closed in Thailand's capital, Bangkok, on 17 October. IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva said low-income countries now spend 14% of government revenue on debt repayments, up from 8%. Reuters says nearly half of delegates walked out while Russia's finance minister spoke.
items.matters: Georgieva calls inflation 'a tax on the poor'; poorer oil-importing countries are hit hardest by the war-driven rise in energy prices.

items.changed: Updated: the Pope led Sunday's Angelus, and his surgeon sees no medical reason to cancel his South America trip
items.title: Pope Leo leads Sunday prayer days after lung cancer surgery
items.why: Pope Leo XIV, 71, led the Angelus prayer from his Vatican window on Sunday, a day after leaving Rome's Gemelli hospital, where part of his right lung was removed on 13 October. He thanked people for their prayers and said he would gradually resume his activities.
items.matters: His surgeon says there is no medical reason to cancel the planned 6 to 17 November trip to South America.

items.changed: Updated: a tug was hit off the UAE on Sunday; Iran says its offer to reopen Hormuz still stands
items.title: Tug hit off UAE as Iran says Hormuz reopening offer still stands
items.why: UKMTO, the UK maritime agency, says two projectiles hit a tug off Khor Fakkan, UAE, on Sunday, injuring one person, after two tankers were attacked off Saudi Arabia on Friday. Iran's foreign minister says Hormuz would reopen within six days if the US lifts its blockade and sanctions.
items.matters: Al Jazeera reports more ships attacked this month than in any month since the Iran war began in February.

items.changed: Updated: about 2,400 arrests, one protester dead, Limoges town hall burned; Macron condemns the violence
items.title: Violent protests sweep France as Macron condemns 'unbridled' violence
items.why: Authorities say 550,000 people protested across France on Saturday over prices and schools. The interior ministry says nearly 2,400 were arrested and about 1,000 police hurt; Limoges's town hall was set alight and one protester died in Paris. President Macron said 'nothing justifies' the violence.
items.matters: The protests, which began in schools in September, are seen as a test of the national mood before the 2027 presidential election.

items.changed: Updated: six more deaths; the toll is now 348, with 103 in October so far
items.title: Bangladesh dengue deaths reach 348 this year as cases pass 112,000
items.why: Bangladesh's health directorate reported six more dengue deaths in the 24 hours to Sunday morning, bringing this year's toll to 348, with 112,400 hospital admissions. October has seen 103 deaths in its first 18 days, after 148 in September, the deadliest month so far.
items.matters: Dengue, spread by mosquitoes, has no specific treatment; Bangladesh's government has ordered neighbourhood awareness campaigns to curb it.

items.changed: Updated: the regional haze alert is at its highest level, and Singapore is acting against seven Indonesian firms
items.title: Indonesia's fires push South-East Asia's haze alert to highest level
items.why: Smoke from Indonesia's worst forest fires in a decade led the regional haze monitor, the ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre, to raise its highest alert for southern South-East Asia on Friday. On Saturday Singapore and Kuala Lumpur were among the world's most polluted major cities, AFP reports.
items.matters: Singapore is serving notices on seven Indonesian companies it links to the fires, ordering them to put the fires out.

items.changed: Updated: Champi passed just south of Guam as a super typhoon; a US emergency declaration was approved
items.title: Super Typhoon Champi skirts Guam, cutting power across much of the island
items.why: The eye of Champi passed about 16 km south of Guam, in the western Pacific, early on Sunday local time as it became a super typhoon, the US National Weather Service says. Early reports show no widespread serious damage, but about half the power network went down.
items.matters: Forecasters expect Champi to stay at super typhoon strength as it heads west across the Philippine Sea this week.

items.changed: Updated: Gulf states pledge to defend Saudi Arabia as Houthi missile and drone attacks continue
items.title: Gulf states back Saudi Arabia as Houthi missile and drone attacks continue
items.why: Gulf Cooperation Council ministers said on Sunday that an attack on any member affects all six, after days of Houthi missiles and drones aimed at Saudi cities. Saudi civil defence says a projectile hurt six people in Najran; Houthi media say Saudi strikes in Yemen killed at least nine.
items.matters: The International Organization for Migration says Yemen's renewed fighting has displaced more than 233,000 people.
